edits.value_json: "四 means ‘four.’ Its current form has enclosing 囗 strokes around inner 儿-form strokes. Its origin is disputed: it may be a direct numeral graph or a graph later borrowed for ‘four.’"

"In its present form, 四 has an enclosing 囗 shape around inner 儿-form strokes; this visible structure does not establish the ancient identities or roles of those parts. Its origin remains disputed. One interpretation reads four horizontal marks as counting rods representing four, while another describes 亖 as a direct numeral graph. A competing proposal treats 四 as a graph depicting breath, identified with 呬, later reused to write ‘four’ because the words may have sounded alike; the original name and pronunciation of the depicted referent are not established. A separate proposal treats 四 as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for ‘four’; this account lacks textual attestation. Neither borrowing explanation is established."

"One interpretation proposes that 四 began as a graph depicting breath, identified with 呬, and was reused to write ‘four’ because the words may have sounded similar. In one reported Old Chinese reconstruction system, 呬 is *hrids and 四 is *hljids. The original name and pronunciation of the proposed breath-related referent are not independently established, and the comparison does not prove that borrowing occurred. Separately, 字源 reports the proposal that 四 was the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for ‘four’; it explicitly notes that this proposal lacks textual attestation."

"For the proposed breath/呬 account, the depicted referent’s original name and pronunciation are not independently established. The reported sound comparison does not prove what the graph depicts or that borrowing occurred. Separately, the 泗 proposal identifies nasal discharge as the proposed referent, but lacks textual attestation."
